_doc: The cheapest meaningful FIRST test for each application that has none. Authored — this half is a judgement and cannot be derived. The countable half (how many shell testers, how many JVM unit source files, whether the ship workflow executes either) IS derived, by cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, which merges the two into 1_cicd/dist/data/test-coverage.json on every `./build.sh workflow`. So the counts here can never drift from the tree: `generated files are up to date` regenerates and compares on every push.
_doc_why: 24 of the 28 ship workflows executed no test of any kind, so for 24 applications the pipeline's only question was 'did Gradle exit 0'. An application with zero testers and one with fifty passing testers produced indistinguishable green ticks, and that indistinguishability is the lie — it is why a feature can be marked done, shipped, and be absent from the phone. Writing 24 test suites is a quarter's work, not a task; naming the gap per application, in data, is what makes the debt legible and orderable.
_doc_first_test: Each note names ONE assertion that needs no emulator, no device and no network — a static check over this application's own source, runnable by cloud-android-test-engine.sh's `shell` phase in seconds. Own source only: a first test that reads another application's tree is downgraded to a warning by the foreign-source rule and can never fail a release.

apps.aa_cloud-superapp: Has 53 shell testers. tests.unit.enabled=false, so its step named 'JVM unit tests (fatal on failure)' executes nothing and goes green — its own task, not this one.
apps.ac_cloud-mail: Has 11 shell testers and 755 JVM unit test classes, both executed. The only application in the fleet whose ship run proves anything beyond compilation.
apps.ac_cloud-writer: Has 6 shell testers, executed. Two prove the routing and the absence of a credential; two prove the four configuration pages exist AND are backed by this app's own store, which is the assertion task 209 lacked; two prove the Material 3 design system is in place and has not been undone — the toolchain restated in build.gradle still matches build.json, no screen draws outside the theme, no hardcoded hex palette or raw-pixel padding has crept back, the price table's cells are still single-line (task 214), and every home-screen card description exists in Spanish (task 221). The gap that remains is that NONE of this is a rendered screen: there is no instrumentation test and no JVM in the container that maintains this app, so a green run proves the APK compiles and the source has the right shape, never that the screen looks right. Only a device screenshot does that.
apps.ac_cloud-me: HAD one tester that no workflow ever called. Now executed, plus a second: the release contract (release.variants[].gh_asset / gh_release.asset_name / phone_install.asset_name / artifact.debug) must name ONE file, or the ship publishes an asset the phone never downloads and every run stays green.
apps.ac_cloud-matrix: 836 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task and let them run — by far the largest untouched suite in the repository, and it needs no new assertion written.
apps.ac_cloud-vault: 634 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Same: declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-media-center: 19 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-nix-on-droid: 21 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-termux: 21 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-dialer: 5 JVM unit test classes have never executed. Declare tests.unit.task.
apps.ac_cloud-browser: COVERED NOW: app/src/test/BrowserFeaturesTest.kt asserts the behaviour of the seven tab features against the SHIPPED build.json::ui.browser - the four first-run tabs arrive pinned and in order, a second launch re-seeds nothing, a pinned tab REFUSES to close, a drag stamps an order that outlives recency, and a non-URL entry resolves to Qwant. test/test-browser-config-boundary.sh holds the #209 line: the shared libs:browser carries none of his URLs and its own default pins nothing, so no other consumer can inherit them. test/test-browser-features-wired.sh proves each feature is reachable from the UI rather than merely modelled. NOT COVERED: nothing instruments the WebView itself. No test loads a page, so a URL that 404s, a viewport that renders blank, or a drag that never fires on real hardware would all still ship green - those need the androidTest source set and a device, and this app has neither.
apps.ac_cloud-calendar: Five-tab WebView shell: assert every tab id in build.json::ui has a data file and every data file a tab — the same page/data drift ac_cloud-me's tester catches.
apps.ac_cloud-news: WebView over topic feeds: assert every topic declared in build.json has a feed URL and no two topics share an id.
apps.ac_cloud-contacts: Assert every channel type a person entry can declare is one the UI knows how to render — an unknown type is a silently blank row.
apps.ac_cloud-wallet: Assert every wallet record type under data/ parses and carries the fields the card renderer requires.
apps.ac_cloud-nav: Assert the Google/OSM module split in settings.gradle matches build.json::modules — a module in one and not the other builds an APK missing a map provider.
apps.ac_cloud-notes: Has 1 shell tester, executed: test-cloud-notes-identity.sh, 9 assertions over a ONE-SHOT VENDORED tree. It guards the two ways a 173-file package rename fails silently. TOO LITTLE: a file the sweep missed keeps the upstream package - a compile error where it is a code reference, but NOT in the manifest, where an un-renamed ContentProvider authority means INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER on the owner's phone the day he also has a real Markor installed, a failure that never happens in CI. TOO MUCH: the sweep also rewrites the Apache-2.0 attribution it is legally required to preserve. It also pins build.json against app/build.gradle (applicationId, versionCode, versionName, and that gradle_task names a flavor this tree actually declares - Markor has THREE, so a task naming none of them is the green-run-that-published-nothing shape). Every assertion was mutation-tested before it was trusted: each was broken on purpose and watched go red, including a control proving the guard does not match its own explanatory comments. THE GAP, NAMED: the vendored tree ships 20 JVM unit test source files under app/src/test/java (GsTextUtilsTest, GsFileUtilsTest, Csv2MdTableTest, the markdown highlighter pattern tests, ...) and NONE of them execute. build.json::tests.unit is disabled deliberately, not by oversight: ship-cloud-notes.yml runs the test-engine step FIRST, before actions/setup-java and setup-android, so that it costs seconds and needs no toolchain - pointing tests.unit.task at a gradle task from there would invoke ./gradlew with no JDK and no Android SDK. Enabling them means moving the unit phase below SDK setup, which every sibling ship workflow would then also want; the task to enable is testFlavorDefaultDebugUnitTest. And nothing here is a rendered screen or an installed APK: no instrumentation test, no JVM in the container that maintains this app, and the phone was unreachable on 2026-09-11, so a green run proves the source has the right shape and never that the editor opens a folder of the owner's markdown.
apps.ac_cloud-camera: Minimal fork of GrapheneOS Camera: assert the patch series applies to the pinned upstream revision, so a silent patch-drop cannot ship an unpatched build.
apps.ac_cloud-ide: Three-app constellation: assert each of the three declares a distinct applicationId and gh_asset, so one fork cannot overwrite another's release asset.
apps.ac_cloud-chat: Fork app: assert build.json::forks.chat's pin and patch list match what materialize-fork resolves, so a moved pin cannot ship unnoticed.
apps.ac_c3-morpheus: WebView panel app: assert every panel endpoint in build.json is a mesh 10.0.0.x address — a public hostname is Authelia-gated and renders a login page on the phone.
apps.ac_c3-watchdog: Same shape as c3-morpheus: assert the dashboard endpoint is a mesh address and the WebView is not pointed at localhost, which inside the app means the phone.
apps.ac_c3-watchtower: Has 1 shell tester (test/test-watchtower-identity.sh): it reads the package id out of this app's own build.json, app/build.gradle, AndroidManifest.xml and MainActivity.kt and asserts all four agree — a typo in any one of them compiles, ships, installs, and leaves the SuperApp's C3 tab opening nothing. It also pins the two ABI variants to distinct asset names, asserts the repo list is read from build.json rather than hardcoded in Kotlin, and forbids /pub/analytics (ingest-only: it would render an empty screen that looks like a network fault). NOT COVERED: nothing executes the app — there is no JVM unit test and no instrumentation, so the arithmetic in Stats (the finished-vs-total denominator) is asserted only as source text, never run. The cheapest next test is a JVM unit test over that reduction with a canned workflow_runs payload; it needs no device and no network, and tests.unit.task is currently undeclared.
apps.ac_cloud-sheets: THREE SHELL TESTERS, ALL NETWORK-BOUND BY NATURE, because every claim this app makes is about a REMOTE object — a pinned Gerrit revision and a sha256-pinned upstream APK. test-configure-flags-exist.sh derives the flag that carries our applicationId from upstream itself and caught --with-android-package-name, which exists nowhere upstream and which autoconf would have warned about and ignored, shipping the megabuild as org.collabora.app. test-engine-artefacts-in-apk.sh range-fetches the pinned APK's central directory and checks every row of tests/engine-artefacts.json, including the load-bearing negative — no .a and no .h anywhere in 6,375 entries. test-no-engine-build-required.sh (2026-09-11) is the one that decides the money: it proves against upstream at the pin that the engine reaches the APK through a jniLibs source dir, that CMake copies it rather than compiling it, that our patch series touches zero native files, and that the COOL bundle target reads no built engine — so #240's ~$35 megabuild is not needed for #224. Its three self-tests break a claim, a comment-only match and the native-file rule on purpose and require each to go red. NOT COVERED, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE GAP: nothing compiles this app. build.host is still null, patches/0002 (the declared --with-prebuilt-engine mode that configure.ac:884 still demands) is not written, and tests/patches-apply.sh proves only that the series APPLIES — it is deliberately not a test-*.sh because it costs a 471 MB Gerrit fetch. No tester here has ever seen this app build, and the artefact on the release shelf is still Collabora's own.
apps.ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks: Assert the per-asset path sets it derives UNION to the workflow's whole trigger list — publish-gate-blast-radius.test.sh already asserts this; give it a tests block so it runs in the ship job too.
apps.ab_cloud-libs-shared/keyboard-engines: Assert the five bundled modules named in build.json all exist under libs/ — a renamed module currently ships a feature pack missing a feature.
apps.a_solutions/ae-tool_termux-boot: Assert the BOOT_COMPLETED receiver is exported and the host package name it reaches matches ac_cloud-nix-on-droid's applicationId; a mismatch is a boot script that silently never runs.
apps.c_devices/garmin-watchface: Assert every design under faces/ is listed in build.json::build.designs and vice versa — a design not listed is never built and never noticed.
apps.ship-firestack-aar.yml: Not an application: publishes the netstack aar the SuperApp pins. It has no WORK_DIR and no publish gate, so it carries neither the test step nor the published-nothing guard. Its 'Guards on the firestack build contract' step is its only assertion.
